title: MetaPI: Constructing Prompt Injection Benchmarks from Any Agent Benchmarks
claim: A modular four-stage pipeline converts any existing agent benchmark into an end-to-end attack evaluation by finding injection points, optimizing payloads, and validating outcomes.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right, four module boxes with a worked example flowing through
description: A horizontal pipeline of four dark-headed modules, M1 to M4, in three columns. M1, Benchmark Connector, shows a victim agent robot exchanging messages with environment icons (terminal, files, shopping, spreadsheet, money). Below that is a numbered list of API calls labeled Unified Trajectory, with venmo.show_transactions highlighted. M2, Strategy Generator, shows an Analyzer that reads the trajectory and environment and produces an Inject Strategy. Below are two dashed boxes: an Inject Position showing transaction records with red injected text, and an Inject Objective in red text. M3, Payload Optimizer, shows a red adversarial payload, a victim agent in an injected environment, and a loop with an LLM Optimizer and response feedback to the attacker LLM. M4, Outcome Validator, re-runs the victim in the injected environment and ends with a gauge icon. Red marks the attack elements. Black arrows link the modules, and the eye starts at M1 at top left.
caption: The METAPI pipeline. Benchmark Connector runs heterogeneous agents and defenses in benchmark environments and records their trajectories in a unified format; Strategy Generator agentically analyzes the trajectory and environment to identify injection positions and generate corresponding attack objectives; Payload Optimizer iteratively searches for effective attack payloads; Outcome Validator re-injects the payloads into the original environment for end-to-end evaluation.
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly perform complex tasks using high-privilege tools, making indirect prompt injection (IPI) a critical security risk. However, IPI benchmarks lag behind their rapidly evolving utility counterparts, only offering limited task and environment coverage and relying on narrow, static attack scenarios. In this paper, we propose meta-benchmarking for IPI: transforming existing utility benchmarks into end-to-end IPI evaluation suites that reuse their realistic tasks, environments, and infrastructure. We present MetaPI, an extensible toolkit that automatically identifies plausible injection points, generates realistic attack objectives, optimizes adaptive payloads, and validates attacks in the real environment. Its modular interfaces support heterogeneous environments, agents, defenses, and attack algorithms, allowing new components to be integrated without redesigning the evaluation pipeline. We apply MetaPI to AppWorld, VitaBench, and Terminal-Bench and evaluate representative agents and defenses across multiple backbone LLMs. Our results show that no evaluated defense simultaneously achieves strong utility and strong security in realistic, adaptive agentic IPI settings. MetaPI thus enables scalable and consistent security evaluation across diverse and evolving agent ecosystems
